question: In which institutions is control moving faster than legal responsibility?
answer: The library tests 15 institutions for practical control running ahead of legal responsibility. The largest group (4) is 'authority contest': IMF surveillance & conditionality; Federal Reserve Payment Account; USAID legal survival / operating death; HHS / proposed AHA. The others: 3 operational test, 1 law ahead of complete operation, 1 proposed adaptation, 1 output shortfall, 1 mixed lag and contest, 1 positive-control candidate, 1 procedural test, 1 governance lag, and 1 positive control (Fedwire ISO 20022), where the legal operator and the records stayed intact. This is the library's lens, not a verdict.

sections.title: What has shifted, across the cases
Case by case
sections.sub: The first lines compare who is legally responsible with who actually runs the thing. Open a card for the counter-reading and what would prove the lens wrong.

items.title: IMF surveillance & conditionality
items.sub: Who defines adjustment, exceptions, and access to Fund money?
kv: Members retain policy authority → IMF staff analyze and negotiate → Executive Board decides reviews, waivers, and purchases
Program conditions and review clocks → National implementation → Household and market incidence
who has the legal mandate; who has a voice; who bears the cost; whether it works; whether people accept it
The IMF’s own framework links perceived evenhandedness to credibility and legitimacy; borrower finance gates differ from advice to nonborrowers.
Output, voice, and burden can converge into legitimacy strain when program adjustment is operationalized without accepted correction.
The distinction follows the lawful difference between surveillance and use of Fund resources; waivers are disclosed and rule-governed.
What would prove the lens wrong
Comparable treatment, measurable outcomes, meaningful member traction, and accepted remedies across a reproducible cohort.
Program cohort, Article IV traction, acceptance, and distributional outcomes.

items.title: Federal Reserve Payment Account
items.sub: Who may admit an institution to central-bank money?
kv: Congressional eligibility → Board policy and general supervision → District Reserve Bank judgment
Primary-supervisor evidence → Bilateral account terms → Monitoring, restriction, or closure
who has the legal mandate; how decisions are made; who has a voice; whether people accept it

Still a proposal (master checked through October 19, 2026). Proposed new Part IV of the Fed's Payment System Risk policy and revised Account Access Guidelines (Docket OP-1878, Federal Register 2026-10375, 91 FR 30627), with amendments to Regulation D (2026-10377) and Regulation A (2026-10376). Board approved May 20, 2026; published May 26, 2026; comments closed July 27, 2026. The Board asked Reserve Banks to pause Tier 3 decisions until it finishes.
Kraken received a narrow one-year Fedwire-only account; the national Payment Account remained proposed at cutoff.
Selective access turns eligibility and institutional consistency into an upstream legitimacy test.
National standards plus local adjudication and strict prefunding may preserve legitimacy rather than weaken it.
What would prove the lens wrong
Clear final criteria, comparable cross-Bank treatment, written reasons, review, and successful bounded operation.
Final OP-1878 disposition, actual use, incidents, reasons, appeal, and cross-Bank consistency.

items.title: GENIUS stablecoin constitution
items.sub: What makes a private dollar claim acceptable, redeemable, and correctable?
kv: Congressional issuer perimeter → Federal, State, or foreign gate → Named issuer and redemption obligation
Reserve manager and custodian → Wallet, exchange, processor, merchant → Redemption, freeze, correction, or insolvency
who has the legal mandate; how decisions are made; who bears the cost; whether it works; whether people accept it
1 final rules and 12 open proposals (master checked through October 21, 2026).
The law creates issuer, reserve, and redemption architecture; a complete approval, operating, and stress chain did not yet exist at cutoff.
A genuine technical money class can outrun the constitution that makes its promise broadly legitimate.
The law may make the technology legible while keeping issuers, reserves, supervisors, and coercive powers named.
What would prove the lens wrong
Rules, approvals, redemption, correction, and insolvency work under consequential scale and stress.
Final rules, first named approval, effective regime, stress redemption, correction, and holder behavior.

items.title: SEC transfer-agent modernization
items.sub: Can distributed execution preserve accountable title and correction?
kv: Securities law and Commission rules → Registered recordkeeping transfer agent → Authoritative master securityholder file
Multichain technical state → Reconciled control book → Correction, examination, and enforcement
who has the legal mandate; whose knowledge counts; how decisions are made; whether it works
The proposal preserves one accountable recordkeeper and master file while permitting linked-DLT systems.
Authoritative-record design can close a capability–structure gap before a public failure tests it.
This may be one of the strongest examples of successful institutional adaptation.
What would prove the lens wrong
A final operating design loses the ability to identify title, reconcile supply, or correct errors.
Comments, final rule, first registered multichain operation, and a public correction case.

items.title: G20 / FSB cross-border payments
items.sub: Who is responsible when global coordination does not reach the end user?
kv: G20 political coordination → FSB and CPMI standards → Domestic law and supervisory bodies
Central-bank and private rails → Correspondents and FX providers → Customer institutions and users
who has a voice; how decisions are made; who bears the cost; whether it works; whether people accept it
FSB monitoring found weak aggregate end-user improvement despite extensive policy milestones.
Output failure becomes a legitimacy problem when coordination lacks delivery authority, user voice, and remedy.
Named corridor governance such as PayNow–PromptPay shows bounded coordination can deliver real gains.
What would prove the lens wrong
Updated KPIs show broad, durable gains with clear finality, recovery, inclusion, and user acceptance.
2026 KPIs, corridor evidence, Nexus operation, fraud, recovery, price, and acceptance.

items.title: Fedwire ISO 20022
items.sub: Can an incumbent public rail modernize without losing its constitution?
kv: Federal Reserve Act and Board supervision → Reserve Banks as legal operators → Reserve Bank account books and finality rules
Federal Reserve Financial Services → ISO 20022 message layer → Participant operations and exceptions
who has the legal mandate; whose knowledge counts; how decisions are made; whether it works; whether people accept it
Production migration completed while legal operator, supervision, authoritative record, and finality remained identifiable.
This weakens a one-way displacement story and tests successful institutional absorption.
Outcome, exception, participant, incident, and cost evidence remains incomplete.
What would prove the lens wrong
Post-cutover failures reveal that nominal authority cannot supervise, reconstruct, or correct the service.
Post-cutover quality, exceptions, incidents, costs, participant experience, and correction data.

items.title: Department of Education distributed operations
items.sub: Can operation move while statutory ownership and borrower remedy remain real?
kv: Congress and statutory charter → Education and Federal Student Aid → Interagency agreements with retained responsibility
Treasury and other operating agencies → Phased service migration → Borrower service, notice, complaint, and remedy
who has the legal mandate; how decisions are made; who bears the cost; whether it works
The charter, appropriation, and no-title-transfer clause remain; full phase operation and borrower outcomes are not proved.
Functional migration tests whether the surviving legal owner can still supervise service and remedy.
Lawful shared services may preserve policy authority while improving continuity.
What would prove the lens wrong
Transparent agreements produce better service with clear ownership, notice, error correction, and appeal.
Phase completion, service, error, complaint, remedy, staffing, and merits evidence.

items.title: USAID legal survival / operating death
items.sub: What remains of a legal institution when its operating body moves?
kv: Congress retains charter and money power → USAID remains a statutory person → State asserts operating control of retained programs
Functions, staff, grants, and contracts move or cease → Liabilities and assets require succession → Beneficiaries experience continuity or loss
who has the legal mandate; who has a voice; how decisions are made; who bears the cost; whether it works
Statutory identity survived while major operating migration was asserted; the complete current census is absent.
Legal survival can coexist with functional hollowing and unresolved responsibility.
The change may be lawful policy reprioritization and consolidation rather than institutional illegitimacy.
What would prove the lens wrong
A lawful, transparent, complete succession preserves service, supervision, liabilities, and remedy.
Succession instruments, operating census, liabilities, continuity, and beneficiary outcomes.

items.title: HHS / proposed AHA
items.sub: Can an announced replacement govern before Congress creates it?
kv: Congress funds HHS components → HHS, SAMHSA, and HRSA remain statutory → Courts review named restructuring actions
AHA announced as an operating box → RIF and partial restructuring → Program continuity and beneficiary effects
who has the legal mandate; who has a voice; how decisions are made; whether it works
Existing components remained statutory and funded; a court preliminarily enjoined named parts of the restructuring.
A proposed operating container can acquire practical weight before its legal person exists.
A final statute, appropriation, or abandoned proposal could resolve the gap through ordinary government process.
What would prove the lens wrong
Congress creates and funds a clear successor, or the proposal is abandoned with complete operational restoration.
Statute or abandonment, operating chart, final judgment, and program continuity.

items.title: OPM central personnel governor
items.sub: Where does personnel authority sit when standards, platforms, and appeals centralize?
kv: Congressional civil-service law → OPM and OMB standards → Employing-agency personnel action → MSPB and courts
Common policies and commercial platforms → Shared service operation → Agency implementation and employee experience
who has the legal mandate; whose knowledge counts; how decisions are made; whether it works; whether people accept it
Policies, awards, and platforms are proved; production migrations, outcomes, AI validation, and appeals are uneven.
Central control may expand faster than responsibility and review can be located in actual cases.
Centralization may improve fragmented systems while independent review supplies a real leash.
What would prove the lens wrong
Production evidence shows clear delegations, improved service, validated tools, and timely effective appeals.
Migrations, decommissioning, service/error data, AI validation, and appeal outcomes.

items.title: OPM digital retirement
items.sub: Does digital intake reduce delay without weakening adjudication and appeal?
kv: OPM retirement mandate → OPM case record and adjudication → Reconsideration and appeal
Agency and payroll inputs → Online Retirement Application → Electronic intake and case routing
how decisions are made; who bears the cost; whether it works; whether people accept it
Use became mandatory for covered groups; OPM reported high electronic intake and substantial throughput.
Real adoption can strengthen legitimacy if it reduces handoff ambiguity while preserving review and correction.
The operating evidence remains issuer-reported and does not establish independent quality or accessibility.
What would prove the lens wrong
Independent evidence finds delay, error, exclusion, privacy, appeal, or outage performance materially worsens.
Independent time, error, backlog, accessibility, privacy, appeal, and outage measures.

items.title: FAR overhaul
items.sub: What governs when operative deviations outrun the public-law rewrite?
kv: Statute and codified FAR → Issued agency deviation → Solicitation and contract → GAO and Court of Federal Claims
Model class deviations → Nonmandatory companion guides → Acquisition workforce practice
who has the legal mandate; how decisions are made; who has a voice; whether it works
Agency deviations can operate before final rulemaking; companion guides can shape practice without independent enforceability.
Implementation speed can widen the gap between practical instruction and public procedural legitimacy.
Rapid simplification can coexist with statutes, protest rights, and eventual rulemaking.
What would prove the lens wrong
Final rules, review decisions, and measured outcomes show a clear, fair, and effective authority chain.
Final rules, adoption census, first protest holdings, competition, speed, price, and performance.

items.title: Treasury / IRS externalized interfaces
items.sub: How far can tax operations move outward while sovereign responsibility stays public?
kv: Treasury and IRS statutory authority → Taxpayer account and confidentiality → Notice, appeal, and judicial review
CEO and Fiscal Service layers → Software, scanning, collection, bank, and processor interfaces → Filing, payment, refund, and contact
who has the legal mandate; how decisions are made; who bears the cost; whether it works; whether people accept it
Selective external operation and capacity contraction are documented; blanket tax-sovereignty transfer is not.
Interface dependence and record-control weakness can decouple practical operation from public accountability.
Bounded vendors may extend capacity while IRS retains assessment, records, confidentiality, and appeal.
What would prove the lens wrong
Delegations, contracts, records, service outcomes, privacy controls, and remedies are complete and effective.
Delegation, contracts, filing/refund/collection outcomes, privacy/error records, and sharing inventory.

items.title: Treasury Do Not Pay
items.sub: Can machine-assisted screening remain a signal rather than a hidden sovereign decision?
kv: Program eligibility authority → Program decision, notice, and appeal → Source-owner record correction
Source datasets → Treasury match or alert → Independent verification → Payment, recovery, or reversal
whose knowledge counts; how decisions are made; who bears the cost; whether it works

September 30, 2026: Treasury reported the process fully operational on September 30 and said it screened 1.1 billion FY2026 payment requests totaling about $3.7 trillion and returned 13,500 deceased-recipient requests totaling $175 million.
DNP is a shared signal; paying programs retain substantive decisions and source owners retain correction duties.
Screening becomes an upstream control point if the signal quietly acquires decisional weight beyond its legal role.
Explicit firewalls, program responsibility, and correction routes are real legitimacy-preserving architecture.
What would prove the lens wrong
Audited cases show independent verification, clear notice, effective appeal, fast source correction, and bounded decisional weight.
End-to-end cases, false-positive rates, decisional weight, logs, correction latency, and audited savings.

items.title: Federal AI / NARA records
items.sub: Can an affected person reconstruct and contest a machine-assisted government action?
kv: Agency mission authority → Agency action and named human responsibility → NARA records requirements → Review and appeal
Vendor models and data → Prompts, outputs, logs, and overrides → Human use under time and workflow constraints
who has the legal mandate; whose knowledge counts; how decisions are made; who bears the cost; whether it works; whether people accept it
AI adoption is real and uneven; NARA guidance defines when AI materials become federal records through capture, use, reliance, and control.
Decision power becomes difficult to justify or remedy when the model-assisted evidentiary chain does not survive.
AI can improve consistency, access, and speed when inputs, tests, outputs, overrides, notice, and appeal are captured.
What would prove the lens wrong
Representative operating evidence shows inspectable models and logs, meaningful human judgment, notice, correction, and independent outcomes.
Decision chains, subgroup tests, versions, override rates, notice, appeals, incidents, and vendor export rights.

uncertain: The lens is a project inference, not a phrase sources must use and not a system-wide verdict. Technology advance, restructuring, litigation, criticism, and output failure do not independently prove legitimacy loss.

The cases carry no official source links of their own and no row dates; the registry's cutoff is September 2, 2026. Three cards (the Fed payment account, the GENIUS Act and Do Not Pay) add the newer master record, which is later than the registry.
'The library's inference' and the state of each case are Katie's research reading, kept beside the other reading and the rival explanation.
